And when the servant went out,
he found Dubais striking his finger upon the ground and saying,
"Death is better than a life without rest."
And he handed him the letter.
And when he took it, opened it, and began to read,
the servant struck him with a sword upon his neck from behind him,
and cut off his head.
And this was the end of Dubais, a shrewd and warlike man.
Now he was killed thirty-five days after the murder of the Caliph al-Mustarshid, his enemy.
And in the year five hundred and thirty,
530 of the Arabs,
which is the year one thousand four hundred and forty-seven,
1447 of the Greeks,
Michael the Armenian—
he who in the days of Balak had sold the fortress of Gargar to the Franks and gone out of it—
turned and stole it away from them.
And he provoked them,
and he used to plunder their villages.
And on one of the days, the Turks overtook Michael the Armenian in the village of Khor Zizona,
which is on the bank of the Euphrates.
And when they surrounded him on every side,
and he was not able to escape,
he threw himself from the cliff into the river.
And because he was wearing a coat of mail of iron,
he sank to the bottom of the water.
And again he came up,
and by means of a ford {or crossing} that was there, he escaped,
and did not die.
It is said
that he did not even drop the shield that was in his hand.
Then he gave Gargar to Joscelin the Second,
and took a place from him called Sophrus.
And Joscelin sold Gargar to Basil, the brother of the Catholicos of the Armenians.
And Michael gathered a force,
and entered and plundered the country of Kaysum.
And the Franks laid an ambush for him and killed him.
And Lord Basil went to Leo in Cilicia,
and became his son-in-law.
And he gathered Armenians and came to make war with the Franks of Kafar Zaman,
and many of the Armenians were killed.
In this year, in the Later Kanun (January), there was a severe cold,
such that mountain birds, partridges and the like,
and even wild animals,
such as stags and the like, would flee and enter the cities,
especially into the city of Amid.
And the ruler commanded
that no one should harm them.
And they used to give them sustenance as long as they were secluded,
and then he released them.
It is said
that before the cold occurred,
from the Tishris (autumn) the birds and animals began to enter into the caves.
